title: Three-tier web app on Kubernetes
summary: A web front end, an API and a database, run as Deployments behind one entry point.
diagram:
title: Three-tier web app on Kubernetes
node: user | Browser | 0 | 1 | Sends requests to the public hostname. | If DNS or the certificate is wrong, nobody gets in. | client
node: ing | Ingress | 1 | 1 | Terminates TLS and routes by host and path. | A bad rule sends traffic to nothing; one controller is a single point of failure. | edge
node: web | Web Pods | 2 | 0 | Serve the front end; stateless, so they scale out. | A failing readiness probe removes Pods from rotation. | service
node: api | API Pods | 2 | 2 | Run the business logic behind a ClusterIP Service. | Missing resource limits let one Pod starve its neighbours. | service
node: db | PostgreSQL | 3 | 2 | Keeps the data on a persistent volume. | Losing the volume without a backup loses the data. | store
node: cache | Redis | 3 | 1 | Caches hot reads to take load off the database. | A cold or flushed cache sends a sudden burst to the database. | cache
node: mon | Prometheus | 1 | 2 | Scrapes metrics from every layer for alerts. | Without alerts you hear about outages from users. | observe
edge: user | ing | HTTPS
edge: ing | web | route
edge: web | api | call
edge: api | cache | read
edge: api | db | query
edge: mon | api | scrape
tradeoffs: Managed database or in-cluster: managed saves operations work; in-cluster keeps everything portable.
One Ingress is simple; several isolate teams but add cost.
breaks: Database pod rescheduled without its volume: data appears empty.
Ingress controller down: the whole site is unreachable although every Pod is healthy.

title: Event-driven pipeline
summary: Producers publish events to a queue; independent consumers process them at their own pace.
diagram:
title: Event-driven pipeline
node: prod | Order service | 0 | 1 | Creates an event for each order. | If it publishes before the database commit, events describe orders that do not exist. | service
node: q | Message broker | 1 | 1 | Holds events durably until consumers take them. | If it is full or down, producers block or lose events. | queue
node: pay | Payment worker | 2 | 0 | Charges the card for each order event. | A retry without an idempotency key charges twice. | service
node: mail | Email worker | 2 | 1 | Sends the confirmation message. | A slow mail provider builds a backlog but should not block orders. | service
node: dlq | Dead-letter queue | 2 | 2 | Receives events that failed repeatedly. | Nobody reading it means failures are silent. | queue
node: db | Orders database | 3 | 0 | Stores the result of processing. | Two workers updating the same row need locking. | store
node: mon | Lag dashboard | 3 | 2 | Shows consumer lag and the dead-letter depth. | No lag alert means a stuck consumer goes unnoticed. | observe
edge: prod | q | publish
edge: q | pay | consume
edge: q | mail | consume
edge: pay | db | write
edge: pay | dlq | fail
edge: dlq | mon | alert

learn.why: Brokers, ordering, retries and dead letters

tradeoffs: At-least-once delivery needs idempotent consumers; exactly-once is costly.
Ordering per key limits parallelism.
breaks: Poison message blocks a partition until it is moved to the dead-letter queue.
Consumer lag grows silently when a worker hangs.

title: Highly available web on AWS
summary: Spread across two Availability Zones so the loss of one data centre does not take the site down.
diagram:
title: Highly available web on AWS
node: dns | Route 53 | 0 | 1 | Maps the name to the load balancer. | A low-health check lets traffic go to a dead endpoint. | edge
node: alb | Load balancer | 1 | 1 | Spreads requests across healthy instances in both zones. | Misconfigured health checks drain good instances. | edge
node: a | App in zone A | 2 | 0 | Instances in an Auto Scaling group. | If both zones share one subnet, the design is not really multi-AZ. | service
node: b | App in zone B | 2 | 2 | The second copy that keeps serving if A fails. | Not enough spare capacity: the surviving zone cannot take all the traffic. | service
node: rds | RDS Multi-AZ | 3 | 1 | Primary with a synchronous standby in another zone. | Failover takes about a minute; apps must reconnect. | store
node: iam | IAM roles | 1 | 0 | Give instances only the access they need. | A wide policy turns one leak into a full breach. | security
node: cw | CloudWatch | 1 | 2 | Alarms on errors, latency and healthy host count. | No alarm on healthy hosts means a half-dead fleet goes unseen. | observe
edge: dns | alb | resolve
edge: alb | a | forward
edge: alb | b | forward
edge: a | rds | query
edge: b | rds | query
edge: cw | alb | alarm

learn.why: Load balancers, zones and Auto Scaling

tradeoffs: Multi-AZ doubles cost for resilience; a single AZ is cheaper but fragile.
Multi-region adds more resilience and much more complexity.
breaks: An AZ fails and the remaining zone is already at 90 percent load.
Database failover works but the application keeps old connections.

title: CI/CD to Kubernetes
summary: Code goes from commit to production through automated tests, an image build and a rollout.
diagram:
title: CI/CD to Kubernetes
node: git | Source repository | 0 | 1 | Holds code and pipeline definition. | Unprotected main branch lets untested code ship. | external
node: ci | CI runner | 1 | 1 | Builds, tests and scans on every change. | A flaky test makes people ignore red builds. | process
node: reg | Image registry | 2 | 0 | Stores signed, versioned images. | Using the latest tag makes rollbacks guesswork. | store
node: scan | Security scan | 2 | 2 | Checks the image and dependencies for known flaws. | Scanning but never failing the build changes nothing. | security
node: cd | Deploy controller | 3 | 1 | Applies the new version to the cluster. | Deploying straight from a laptop skips every check. | process
node: k8s | Cluster | 4 | 1 | Rolls out with probes and keeps the old version until the new is ready. | No readiness probe means traffic reaches a Pod that is not ready. | service
node: obs | Monitoring | 4 | 2 | Watches error rate after release for a fast rollback. | No automatic rollback leaves users on a broken release. | observe
edge: git | ci | push
edge: ci | reg | push image
edge: ci | scan | scan
edge: reg | cd | new tag
edge: cd | k8s | rollout
edge: k8s | obs | metrics
tradeoffs: Push-based CD is simple; pull-based keeps the cluster the source of truth.
More gates mean safer releases and slower feedback.
breaks: A bad config passes tests but fails in the cluster; only a readiness probe catches it.
The registry is down and new Pods cannot pull the image.

title: Observability stack
summary: Metrics, logs and traces from every service, with alerts that page the right person.
diagram:
title: Observability stack
node: app | Applications | 0 | 1 | Emit metrics, structured logs and trace spans. | Unstructured logs cannot be searched at 3 a.m. | service
node: prom | Prometheus | 1 | 0 | Scrapes and stores metrics. | High-cardinality labels can exhaust its memory. | observe
node: logs | Log store | 1 | 1 | Collects and indexes logs. | Keeping everything forever gets expensive fast. | store
node: trace | Tracing backend | 1 | 2 | Follows one request across services. | Without sampling, tracing costs more than the app. | observe
node: graf | Dashboards | 2 | 1 | Show the health of the whole system. | A wall of graphs nobody understands hides the real signal. | client
node: alert | Alertmanager | 3 | 0 | Groups and routes alerts to on-call. | Alerts on causes instead of symptoms cause fatigue. | queue
node: oncall | On-call engineer | 4 | 0 | Gets paged, follows a runbook. | No runbook turns every page into guesswork. | external
edge: app | prom | scrape
edge: app | logs | ship
edge: app | trace | spans
edge: prom | graf | query
edge: logs | graf | query
edge: prom | alert | rules
edge: alert | oncall | page
tradeoffs: Managed observability saves effort; self-hosted gives control and lower cost at scale.
Page on symptoms such as errors and latency, ticket on causes.
breaks: The monitoring system runs on the cluster it monitors and dies with it.
A silent exporter looks like a healthy service.

title: Secrets with Vault on Kubernetes
summary: Pods get short-lived credentials from Vault instead of long-lived secrets in manifests.
diagram:
title: Secrets with Vault on Kubernetes
node: pod | App Pod | 0 | 1 | Authenticates with its service account. | A shared service account lets any Pod read any secret. | service
node: auth | Kubernetes auth | 1 | 1 | Vault checks the account token with the API server. | A wide role binding gives away more than intended. | security
node: vault | Vault cluster | 2 | 1 | Issues secrets according to policy. | Sealed or unreachable Vault stops new credentials. | security
node: pol | Policy | 2 | 0 | Says which paths each role can read. | A wildcard policy defeats least privilege. | security
node: db | Database engine | 3 | 1 | Creates a unique database user for each lease. | Leases that never expire keep dead users alive. | store
node: audit | Audit log | 2 | 2 | Records every request, who and what. | Logs sent nowhere cannot support an investigation. | observe
node: raft | Raft storage | 3 | 2 | Replicates Vault data across three nodes. | Losing quorum makes Vault read-only or down. | store
edge: pod | auth | token
edge: auth | vault | validate
edge: pol | vault | enforce
edge: vault | db | create user
edge: vault | audit | log
edge: vault | raft | store
tradeoffs: Dynamic secrets limit damage but add a runtime dependency on Vault.
Sidecar injection is simple; CSI avoids extra containers.
breaks: Vault restarts and stays sealed: no Pod can start new connections.
A leaked token with a long TTL stays valid until revoked.

title: VMs and containers on one platform
summary: KubeVirt runs virtual machines beside containers, on storage that Ceph provides.
diagram:
title: VMs and containers on one platform
node: ctl | Kubernetes API | 1 | 0 | One control plane for Pods and VMs. | An unhealthy control plane stops changes, not running guests. | service
node: kv | KubeVirt | 1 | 1 | Turns a VirtualMachine into a KVM guest in a Pod. | Missing virtualization on the node leaves VMs pending. | service
node: vm | Guest VM | 2 | 1 | Runs the legacy application as before. | Without live migration support, node updates mean downtime. | service
node: pod | Container apps | 2 | 0 | Modern services next to the VMs. | Noisy neighbours without limits slow the VMs. | service
node: rook | Rook | 1 | 2 | Operates Ceph inside the cluster. | Rook upgrades must follow Ceph rules. | process
node: ceph | Ceph RBD | 2 | 2 | Block volumes that follow the VM to any node. | Near-full pools turn writes read-only. | store
node: net | Multus network | 3 | 1 | Gives VMs secondary networks and VLANs. | Wrong bridge settings isolate the VM. | edge
edge: ctl | kv | CRDs
edge: kv | vm | launch
edge: ctl | pod | schedule
edge: vm | ceph | disk
edge: rook | ceph | operate
edge: vm | net | attach
tradeoffs: One platform lowers tooling cost; separate stacks isolate risk.
Live migration needs shared ReadWriteMany or block storage.
breaks: Node drain evicts VMs that cannot live-migrate.
Ceph fills after one failure because there was no spare capacity.

title: Edge, CDN and reverse proxy
summary: Requests are cached at the edge, protected, then balanced to origin servers.
diagram:
title: Edge, CDN and reverse proxy
node: user | Visitor | 0 | 1 | Requests a page from anywhere. | Distance and slow networks hurt speed. | client
node: cdn | CDN | 1 | 1 | Serves cached content near the visitor. | A wrong cache key shows one user another user's page. | edge
node: waf | WAF and rate limits | 2 | 0 | Blocks known attacks and floods. | Strict rules block real customers. | security
node: rp | Reverse proxy | 2 | 1 | Terminates TLS and routes to backends. | Missing timeouts let slow clients hold connections. | edge
node: app1 | Origin A | 3 | 0 | One backend instance. | If only one origin exists, the proxy cannot help. | service
node: app2 | Origin B | 3 | 2 | A second instance for balance and failover. | Sticky sessions make uneven load. | service
node: log | Access logs | 2 | 2 | Record every request for debugging. | No request ID makes tracing hard. | observe
edge: user | cdn | request
edge: cdn | waf | miss
edge: waf | rp | allow
edge: rp | app1 | balance
edge: rp | app2 | balance
edge: rp | log | log
tradeoffs: Cache aggressively for speed; cache carefully for correctness.
A managed edge is easy; a self-run proxy gives control.
breaks: Origin outage with a short cache TTL: the CDN passes the failure to everyone.
Large uploads hit a default body size limit.

title: Backup and disaster recovery
summary: Three copies, two media and one off-site, with restores that are tested.
diagram:
title: Backup and disaster recovery
node: prod | Production data | 0 | 1 | The live system. | Replication copies deletions and corruption too. | store
node: snap | Snapshots | 1 | 0 | Fast local recovery points. | On the same storage, a storage failure loses both. | store
node: bk | Backup job | 1 | 2 | Copies data to another system on a schedule. | A job that fails silently leaves no backup. | process
node: off | Off-site copy | 2 | 2 | Stored in another region or provider, immutable. | Same credentials as production let an attacker delete it. | external
node: rest | Restore test | 3 | 1 | Regular rebuild in a clean environment. | An untested backup is only a hope. | process
node: rto | Runbook | 3 | 0 | Steps, owners and targets for recovery time. | An out-of-date runbook costs hours. | observe
node: dr | DR site | 2 | 1 | Warm standby in another region. | Never failed over means you do not know it works. | service
edge: prod | snap | snapshot
edge: prod | bk | copy
edge: bk | off | replicate
edge: off | rest | restore
edge: rest | rto | measure
edge: prod | dr | replicate
tradeoffs: Lower RTO and RPO cost more; decide what an hour of downtime really costs.
Warm standby recovers faster than rebuild-from-backup, at higher cost.
breaks: Ransomware encrypts production and the connected backup together.
The restore works but takes 14 hours when the target was 2.

title: Hybrid network: on premises and cloud
summary: A private link joins the office network to the cloud, with DNS and routing that work both ways.
diagram:
title: Hybrid network: on premises and cloud
node: onp | On-premises network | 0 | 1 | Office and data-centre servers. | Overlapping IP ranges make routing impossible. | external
node: fw | Firewall | 1 | 1 | Controls what crosses the link. | Allow-all rules defeat the point of a private link. | security
node: vpn | VPN or direct link | 2 | 1 | The encrypted or dedicated connection. | A single tunnel is a single point of failure. | edge
node: tgw | Cloud router | 3 | 1 | Routes between VPCs and the link. | Missing route entries create one-way traffic. | edge
node: vpc | Cloud network | 4 | 0 | Private subnets for the workloads. | Public subnets by accident expose servers. | service
node: dns | Hybrid DNS | 2 | 0 | Resolves names in both directions. | Split-brain DNS sends users to the wrong address. | edge
node: mon | Link monitoring | 2 | 2 | Tracks latency, loss and tunnel state. | No monitoring means you learn from a call. | observe
edge: onp | fw | traffic
edge: fw | vpn | encrypt
edge: vpn | tgw | route
edge: tgw | vpc | deliver
edge: dns | vpn | resolve
edge: mon | vpn | probe
tradeoffs: VPN is cheap and quick; a dedicated link gives steady latency at higher cost.
Two links in different paths remove the single point of failure.
breaks: Both tunnels share one device and fail together.
Route advertisements overlap and traffic loops.

title: Retrieval-augmented AI service
summary: An LLM answers from your own documents by retrieving the relevant passages first.
diagram:
title: Retrieval-augmented AI service
node: user | User question | 0 | 1 | Asks in natural language. | Ambiguous questions need a clarifying step. | client
node: gw | API gateway | 1 | 1 | Authenticates, rate-limits and logs. | No limits turn one bug into a large bill. | edge
node: emb | Embedding model | 2 | 0 | Turns the question into a vector. | A different model than the index gives poor matches. | service
node: vec | Vector store | 3 | 0 | Finds the closest document chunks. | Stale index returns outdated answers. | store
node: llm | Language model | 3 | 1 | Writes an answer from the question and passages. | May invent facts when the passages are weak. | service
node: guard | Guardrails | 2 | 2 | Filter prompt injection and unsafe output. | Trusting retrieved text as instructions is an attack path. | security
node: eval | Evaluation and logs | 4 | 1 | Samples answers and scores quality. | Without evaluation, quality drift goes unnoticed. | observe
edge: user | gw | ask
edge: gw | emb | embed
edge: emb | vec | search
edge: vec | llm | context
edge: guard | llm | check
edge: llm | eval | sample
tradeoffs: Bigger context windows reduce retrieval needs but cost more per call.
Fine-tuning changes style; retrieval keeps facts fresh.
breaks: The index is not updated and the model confidently quotes last year's policy.
A retrieved web page contains instructions the model obeys.
